        If I do not recognize the pattern, I then activate my search tools: I generate vector representations (embeddings) and look for the most relevant fragments across multiple documents—including the report itself, external PDF and HTML files, and question-and-answer (QA) sessions.  
        Based on that information, I create a summary that aims to provide you with a coherent and useful response grounded in the existing content.
      </p>

      <p>
        Please note that this environment is experimental. I do not use large language models, so some responses may be approximate or incomplete.  
        The main goal is to provide a fast, understandable, and reproducible way to visualize the information contained in the documents, enabling a more dynamic exploration of the report.
      </p>

      <p>
        Currently, results may vary in accuracy, as I use lightweight local models to ensure the application runs in any environment without the need for external servers.  
        However, the system structure is designed to significantly improve its performance in the future through integration with more advanced models or external APIs.  
        To get started, simply type your question in the field below and let me take care of the rest. I promise to put all my code into it!
      </p>

<div class="informe-resumen">
  <h2>Conclusions and perspectives</h2>

  <p>
    This final section serves to <strong>close and integrate the set of analyses presented throughout the 16S metagenomic report</strong>. Rather than listing specific findings, it aims to provide a <strong>global and contextualized view</strong> of the results obtained, highlighting their relevance within the experimental framework and their potential to generate new research questions.
  </p>

  <p>
    Based on taxonomic characterization, the evaluation of microbial diversity, and the comparative analyses performed, it is possible to <strong>outline general interpretations</strong> regarding microbial dynamics under the studied conditions. These reflections allow the results to be placed in a broader biological context, without losing sight of the inherent limitations of the approach used and the need for complementary analyses.
  </p>

  <p>
    Finally, this section <strong>opens the door to future developments</strong>, such as experimental validation of observed patterns, integration with other types of data (multi-omics, environmental, clinical, or phenotypic), and the exploration of new hypotheses derived from the present study. In this way, the report is not only concluded, but also lays the foundation for <strong>future research lines and applications</strong>.
  </p>
</div>

<div class="titulo1" id="tab3-seccion6">
  8<span>.</span> Conclusions and perspectives
</div>

<p>
  Throughout this report, a comprehensive <strong>16S metagenomic analysis</strong> has been conducted, systematically covering all essential stages of a typical workflow in microbial characterization studies based on amplicon sequencing. 
  From the <strong>initial review of samples and their metadata</strong>, through the <strong>quality control of raw reads</strong>, the <strong>generation of ASVs and abundance tables</strong>, the <strong>taxonomic and phylogenetic assignment</strong>, and the <strong>microbial diversity analyses</strong>, to the <strong>functional prediction of metabolic pathways</strong>, each step has been implemented with a rigorous, reproducible approach oriented toward biological interpretation.
</p>

<p>
  The <strong>initial review</strong> ensured consistency between samples, their experimental conditions, and associated metadata, providing a solid foundation for downstream analyses. The <strong>quality control and preprocessing procedures</strong> helped remove low-quality reads, minimizing biases and strengthening the robustness of the final sequence dataset used.
</p>

<p>
  Through <strong>taxonomic assignment</strong> and the <strong>construction of the abundance table</strong>, a detailed characterization of the microbial communities present in the samples was obtained. The <strong>alpha and beta diversity analyses</strong> revealed patterns of richness, evenness, and differentiation between experimental groups, providing a comprehensive ecological view of the microbial communities.
</p>

<p>
  In turn, the <strong>differential abundance analysis</strong> allowed the identification of taxa with significantly different patterns between conditions, providing evidence of <strong>potential microbial associations with biological or environmental variables</strong>. 
  The <strong>functional prediction</strong> using tools such as <code>PICRUSt2</code> complemented this taxonomic view with information on possible <strong>metabolic functions and biological pathways</strong> involved in the observed differences, enriching the ecological and functional interpretation of the study.
</p>

<p>
  Overall, this report constitutes a <strong>comprehensive analytical platform</strong> for the exploration and contextualization of microbial communities using 16S sequencing techniques. 
  Its results not only allow the characterization of the structure and potential function of the analyzed microbiomes, but also provide a solid foundation for <strong>biological hypothesis generation</strong> and the planning of further studies.
</p>

<p>
  As future directions, the following recommendations are suggested:
</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Experimentally validate taxa or functions of interest</strong> using complementary techniques such as targeted qPCR, specific culturing, or metabolomic analyses.
  </li>
  <li>
    Incorporate <strong>environmental, phenotypic, or clinical data</strong> to explore correlations and generate more comprehensive explanatory models.
  </li>
  <li>
    Develop <strong>microbial network analyses</strong> to identify potential interactions between taxa and complex community structures.
  </li>
  <li>
    Move toward <strong>multi-omics approaches</strong> (e.g., shotgun metagenomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) that provide deeper functional resolution.
  </li>
  <li>
    Apply <strong>advanced computational models</strong> and robust statistical methods to identify non-obvious ecological patterns and improve the predictive power of the analysis.
  </li>
</ul>

<p>
  In summary, this analysis represents a fundamental step toward the <strong>ecological and functional understanding of the studied microbial communities</strong>, and lays the groundwork for more specific, integrative, and complex future research aimed at addressing higher-level biological or biotechnological questions.
</p>

<div class="titulo3" id="tab3-soporte">
  ➤ Support and Contact
</div>

<p>
  Amplicon metagenomic analysis generates a vast data ecosystem with high technical complexity. We understand that digesting this information and integrating it with laboratory results is an ongoing process. 
</p>

<p>
  Therefore, for any methodological questions, inquiries regarding the interpretation of results, or the need to explore the data from new perspectives, the <strong>Bioinformatics Unit</strong> team is fully available. We will be happy to assist you in the optimal exploitation of this resource and in the planning of your future research directions.
</p>
